headline: Application Support Engineer | Linux | AWS | SQL
summary: Cloud and DevOps Engineer who troubleshoots from evidence rather than guesswork: decoded a live GitHub OIDC token to fix an AWS trust-policy failure, traced an AWS AuthFailure to clock skew from blocked NTP, and writes incident reports with root cause and corrective actions. Operates an enterprise-style RHEL environment through tickets and runbooks, and works with Linux, SQL, REST APIs and AWS.

bullets.text: Completed 30 hands-on labs across build tools (Gradle, Maven), Docker, Jenkins, Kubernetes, ArgoCD and Ansible, each documented with its objective, steps and verification.
Completed intensive hands-on training in Linux administration, networking, CI/CD, containerization, and cloud infrastructure, culminating in end-to-end DevOps projects (see Projects).

bullets.label: Identity & Team Policy
bullets.text: FreeIPA centralizes users, DNS, Kerberos, HBAC and sudo rules per team; the utility server runs a Squid proxy with per-team internet rules, NFS home directories, centralized logging and backups.

bullets.label: Automation & Operations
bullets.text: Idempotent Ansible roles (EC2 dynamic inventory) handle SSH hardening, SELinux, firewalld, chrony and fleet patching; Bash scripts rebuild and test the lab, with tickets, runbooks and incident reports documenting changes.

bullets.label: Platform & Security
bullets.text: Five Python/FastAPI banking microservices and an NGINX frontend on EKS, built for financial correctness (fencing tokens, row-lock ordering). Versioned Terraform modules deploy through GitHub Actions (OIDC) and ArgoCD App-of-Apps, secured with default-deny NetworkPolicies, Istio mTLS, Gateway API and External Secrets Operator (IRSA).

Declared observability as code with 12 Prometheus alert rules each backed by a runbook, three Grafana dashboards, Fluent Bit shipping JSON logs with correlation IDs to Loki, and OpenTelemetry traces in Tempo.
Fixed a GitHub Actions OIDC trust-policy failure by decoding the live JWT, finding the immutable numeric IDs in its sub claim, and building the correct wildcard with Terraform replace().
Resolved a kube-prometheus-stack ArgoCD sync failure caused by the Kubernetes 262144-byte annotation limit by enabling ServerSideApply.
Wrote a failure test that stops a backend, measures traffic continuing on the healthy instances, restores it and proves recovery, plus backup and restore of the database.
Containerized a Flask API as three non-root instances behind an NGINX reverse proxy load balancer, backed by PostgreSQL on a persistent volume, with health checks on every container.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Application Support Engineer role at Pyramid Pay. I solve infrastructure problems methodically and document them so they stay solved. I work from logs and evidence, using Linux, SQL, REST APIs and AWS.

You ask for Linux and log analysis. In my RHEL lab, with FreeIPA identity, a VPN and a Squid proxy, I ran incident drills for an identity outage, a full log disk and a package rollback, documented in 7 incident reports with root cause and actions. I also traced a Terraform AWS AuthFailure to about 14 minutes of clock skew from blocked outbound NTP. For SQL and REST APIs, I built Python/FastAPI services on MySQL in the Nexora banking platform, with Pytest integration tests.

Troubleshooting is the part of the work I already do every day: reading logs, narrowing a cause with evidence, fixing it, and writing the runbook. A support role puts that skill directly in front of users and production systems. My lab changes go through tickets and runbooks, though I have not used Jira itself yet. I would welcome a conversation about the role; my CV is attached.
